pages.title: Chapter 2
pages.description: Yahweh's judgement rests on truth and righteousness. After the thousand years, Jesus judges the living and the dead, and the holy city, new Jerusalem, appears.

headings.name: 1. Yahweh God is the ultimate Judge of Men

columns.title: What makes God’s Judgement unique?
columns.text: :::p:0: It is based on truth and righteousness. Rom 2:2 Rom 2:5

columns.title: When is God’s Judgement?
columns.text: :::p:7: After the great tribulation, Jesus will reigned on earth for 1,000 years, He will put all enemies under His feet and destroy Death. Then the end comes when He delivers the Kingdom to God the Father. 1Co 15:24-26 On judgement day, God will judge men by His Son, Jesus, who died, rose again and became Lord of the living and the dead. Rom 2:16 Rom 14:9

columns.title: What happens next?
columns.text: After Jesus delivers the kingdom to His Father, there will be a great and high mountain, the great city, the holy Jerusalem, with the glory of God. Rev 21:2-3 The nations, of the saved, shall walk in its light, and the kings of the earth will bring their glory and honour into it. Rev 21:24 (From the beginning, God’s plan has always been to save all nations from eternal condemnation.) Nothing shall enter the City that defiles, or causes an abomination or a lie, only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.  Rev 21:27 It is only through the ‘Lamb who was slain and rose from the grave’ that Mankind will be given eternal life. Eternal condemnation awaits those who were not saved. Jhn 3:36

columns.title: Who did Paul accuse of Judging without Excuse?
columns.text: :::p:0: Continuing from the last verse in chapter 1 it is those who: :::p:0: • know the righteous judgement of God :::p:0: • practise things deserving of death :::p:0: • approve of some who do the same :::p:0: • yet judge others who practise such things Rom 1:32 :::p:0: This description fits some scribes and Pharisees whom Jesus judged and some like them may have been in Rome: :::p:0: • Sitting in Moses’ seat but do not do what they teach Mat 23:2-3 :::p:0: • Laying heavy burdens on others which they do not carry themselves Mat 23:4 :::p:0: • Neglecting Justice Mercy and Faith Mat 23:23 :::p:0: • Full of extortion and self-indulgence Mat 23:25 :::p:7: • Serpents, brood of vipers, destined for hell Mat 23:33 :::p:7: Today, this might apply to some religious leaders, politicians, business corporations, mainstream media, internet influencers and fake news. They deceive, mislead, are hypocrites, take advantage of others and lead them away from God’s righteous ways. :::p:0: Paul told Timothy that “All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for: :::p:0: • doctrine, :::p:0: • reproof, (the exposure of error) :::p:0: • correction, (restoring a believer to right standing again) :::p:7: • instruction in righteousness :::p:0: The purpose is: :::p:0: “that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.” 2Ti 3:16-17 You may notice that ‘reproof’ and ‘correction’ actually need some form of judging behaviour.  So how do we reconcile that with: “Why do you judge your brother? Or why do you show contempt for your brother? For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.”? Rom 14:10

columns.title: Judging One Another
columns.text: On the day of Judgement, Jesus the Messiah will judge every human being. This type of judgement is for God and God alone. We are not to judge if anyone is going to be saved or not. However, Paul also gives instructions about people’s behaviour and the appropriate procedures, motivations and actions. :::p:3: 1Ti 5:19-20 :::p:3: 19 Do not entertain an accusation against an elder unless it is brought by two or three witnesses. :::p:7: 20 But those elders who are sinning you are to reprove before everyone, so that the others may take warning. :::p:3: In the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead, and in view of his appearing and his kingdom, :::p:3: I give you this charge: :::p:0: 2Ti 4:2-3 2 Preach the word; be prepared in season and out of season; correct, rebuke and encourage :::p:3: — with great patience and careful instruction. 3 For the time will come when people will not put up with sound doctrine. Instead, to suit their own desires, they will gather around them a great number of teachers to say what their itching ears want to hear. This is not the place to teach about judging sin in others. There is plenty of teaching in the Torah and the New Testament if you follow Paul’s charge. ‘Preach the Word of God and be ready to correct and rebuke.' But remember, only do it to encourage with love in your heart. Check that there is no Judgement in your thoughts before opening your mouth; it may not be appropriate for you to speak or the right moment for them to hear.

Paul refers to God's promises 10 times in Romans, and half of them are in Chapter 4. (You can read them all, if you want to, by clicking on the references.) Unfortunately, most of them did not say what the promises are, apart from: "Abraham and his seed being the heir of the world." 2   and "I have made you a father of many nations" 3  Paul and the Jews in Rome, would have been familiar with God's promises because most of the promises are for them.  Both the Jews and the Gentiles would have been taught which prophecies Jesus had fulfilled. None of them would have read Revelation.   Based on the OT prophecies and the whole of the NT, I put together a short video to give you some idea of how Abraham and his seed may become heirs of the world and how the Gentiles could fit in. I know that Jesus has more prophecies to fulfil, and Abraham and his descendants have not yet inherited the world!   Before we watch it, let's go through what it means for Abraham and his seed/descendants to inherit the world.
1 Rom 1:1-2 2 Rom 4:13-16 3 Rom 4:17-18 4 Rom 4:20-21 5 Rom 9:4 6 Rom 9:8-9 7 Rom 15:8

Time and time again, Yahweh promises, "All the land I give to you and your descendants forever." The scriptures on the right are God's promises to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob about the land. After reading all these 10 verses, I was convinced that Yahweh will keep this promise. It will start when Jesus returns as King of kings and Lord of lords. What else could they all mean?
1 Gen 12:7 2 Gen 13:15-17 3 Gen 15:7 4 Gen 15:18 5 Gen 17:8 6 Gen 26:3 7 Gen 28:13 8 Gen 35:12

headings.name: As the Dust and the Stars

columns.text: Yahweh promised that Abraham's descendant would be like the dust of the earth and the stars in the sky. Paul teaches in Romans that Abraham's believing descendants will inherit the whole world.
1 Gen 13:16 2 Gen 15:5 3 Gen 22:17 4 Gen 26:4 5 Gen 28:14

Yahweh made Abraham father of many nations and promised that kings shall come from him. 1  It does not look like this today, but one day it will be fulfilled. And He said something very personal: "I will be their God." Right at the start of Romans, the good news is about God's Son, born into David's family. It is for the Jew first, and also for the rest of the world. Genesis had already said, "In you all the nations shall be blessed."
1 Gen 17:4-6 2 4-6 3 Rom 4:17-18 4 Gen 17:15-16 5 Gen 35:11 6 Gen 17:7-8 7 Rom 1:1-3 8 Rom 1:16 9 Gen 12:3 10 Gen 18:18 11 Gen 22:18 12 Gen 26:4 13 Gen 28:14 14 Gal 3:8
This week's verse goes even wider. Paul says Abraham would be "heir of the world." Then he says this is for us too. If you belong to Christ, you are Abraham's family, and you share the same promise.
1 Rom 4:13 2 Rom 4:23-24 3 Gal 3:29

God also promised to deal with the things that break us. Christ came to put away sin, and He will come again. Paul calls God the One who "gives life to the dead." He raised Jesus from the dead. Here is the heart of it. The promise is sure, not because we are strong, but because it rests on God. Abraham was fully convinced that what God had promised, He was also able to do. God keeps His word. Let's see what that might look  like.
1 Heb 9:26-28 2 Rom 4:17-19 3 Heb 11:19 4 Rom 4:24 5 Rom 4:16 6 Rom 4:21

headings.name: King of Kings and Lord of Lords

columns.text: <video class="col-vid" src="/sites/Romans/images/king-of-kings-web.mp4" data-speed="100"></video>
The Video is my understanding of how Yahweh's promises could be fulfilled. So what brought me to this particular understanding? Years of reading scriptures from Genesis to Revelation.

In the beginning, God walked with Adam and Eve in a garden, but mankind rebelled and were expelled. Yahweh promised Abraham, "I will be their God." God will live with mankind again. He will wipe away every tear. There will be no more death, and nothing less than perfection. The earth will be made new, like that very first garden was, and this time it will last. It will be a world at peace, with the nations at rest and Yahweh at home with His children.
1 Gen 3:23-24 2 Gen 17:7-8 3 Rev 21:3-4 4 Rev 21:1-3 5 Rev 22:1-3 6 Isa 2:4

One man’s Promise for the whole worldGod’s promise to Abraham family is heir of His kingdom. They will inherit the whole world. This isn't some vague abstract mystery for theologians. A renewed earth will become Yahweh’s home for His family. And if you belong to His Son, Jesus, His home will be for you.
1 Rom 4:13 2 Rom 8:16-17 3 Gal 3:29

Some of us feel a long way from all this. Abraham did too. He waited, and he didn't see the whole promise finished in his lifetime. But he trusted the One who spoke it. We know the end from the beginning because He revealed it in the Bible.
1 Heb 11:8-10 2 Heb 11:13 3 Isa 46:9-10

If your heart is weary and your thoughts are troubled, this is for you. The promise doesn't depend on how strong you feel today or how good you are. It rests on God. The God who gives life to the dead. Abraham looked at his own body, as good as dead, and he still trusted God. And God has already done the greatest by giving us His only begotten Son. Yahweh raised Jesus from the dead as proof. Proof of what?
1 Rom 4:16-17 2 Rom 4:19-21 3 John 3:16 4 Rom 8:32 5 Acts 17:31 6 Rom 4:24-25

The video closed with God's own words: the one who overcomes shall inherit all things. "I will be his God, and he shall be My son." You don't need to be an expert in the future. You do need to know the One who promised you a future. You don’t need to know when it will happen. But like Abraham, you need to know that it will happen. Believe the same God who raised Jesus, He will be back to dwell with His people who are in Christ.
1 Rev 21:7 2 Acts 1:11 3 Rev 21:3
